item: A ratchet classifies every loop in src/database whose back-edge sits outside the cleanup around it, and two comments stop attaching a timing to a size
refs: PR pending; audit 0.5.0 A-012 part 2 and A-027; follows PR #1489 and R234
summary: A-012 part 2: of the loops in src/database whose JUMP_BACKWARD lies outside an enclosing with, try/finally or except BaseException, twelve functions remain after #1489's conversions; each is listed in tests/test_database_loop_heads_are_classified.py with who runs it (worker-only or event-loop) and none is reachable by a main-thread KeyboardInterrupt, so no conversion is owed. The test fails on a new such head without a row and on a stale row, and an anti-vacuity test pins the shapes it reads. The worker-only classification rests on callers found by grep, not on thread starts traced line by line; scripts/signal_leak_probe.py is the one caller outside the server and is a dev probe (inferred, labelled so). A-027: two fts.py comments said 981 s then 1,645 s on a 130 GB corpus; SCALE_ROADMAP P0.4 records two consecutive boots on 2026-07-09 with a database of 11.7 GB and a data folder near 130 GB, so the comments now say that and claim no size the timing follows. Comment-only in src.
